claims.text: Combining Green–Kubo molecular dynamics with DFT-based Boltzmann transport calculations can separately predict lattice and electronic thermal conductivity.
The proposed combined scheme will decouple lattice and electronic heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
Green–Kubo molecular dynamics can be used to calculate lattice thermal conductivity from heat flux.
DFT electronic states coupled to a linearized Boltzmann transport equation can be used to calculate electronic thermal conductivity.
Explicit electron–phonon coupling corrections will improve the accuracy of electronic transport predictions for HfNbTaTiZr.
Isotopic mass substitution changes vibrational dynamics without changing the electronic band structure.
Changes in vibrational density of states caused by isotopic mass substitution isolate the phonon-mediated heat-transport contribution.
Classical molecular dynamics can capture phonon dynamics at any order and can be applied to potentially very large structures.
Accurate interatomic parameters are required for Green–Kubo calculations based on molecular dynamics force fields.
Linearized Boltzmann transport in the relaxation-time approximation has an inherent limitation because the electron lifetime must be determined separately.
Earlier calculations used Debye-model parameters derived from equation-of-state calculations.
Earlier Debye-temperature or simplified DFT estimates inherently conflated lattice and electronic heat transport.
The proposed approach will outperform earlier approaches by resolving electron–phonon interactions and separately calculating lattice and electronic transport.
Isotopic mass variation will reduce the predicted lattice thermal conductivity of pristine HfNbTaTiZr by approximately 10–15% relative to uniform-mass simulations at 300–1200 K.
The calculated electronic contribution will agree with low-temperature HfNbTaTiZr measurements over 50–200 K.
The combined predicted total thermal conductivity will be within approximately 10% of experimental values.
The integrated prediction will improve error by approximately 10% relative to earlier analytical estimates.
The 300–1200 K regime in HfNbTaTiZr is lattice-dominated.
The proposed validity domain is defect-free, high-purity, stoichiometric HfNbTaTiZr from 50 K to 1200 K.
Oxygen or other defects may change both phonon scattering and electronic structure, requiring modification of the model.

contradictions.description: The model is restricted to pristine, defect-free material and explicitly warns that oxygen-doped samples may require modification, but the falsification comparison does not require composition-matched measurements; using the cited high-temperature oxygen-containing specimen as the decisive comparison would fall outside the stated validity domain.
